title: UTC-session VWAP 2-sigma lower-band fade on 15m: close back inside the band, exit at VWAP, flat by day end
ex_ante_rule: Chart 15m, closed bars only, all times UTC. A signal at the close of bar t fills at the open of bar t+1. Warm-up: 192 bars. SESSION: each UTC day; it resets at 00:00 UTC. For every bar, typical price tp=(high+low+close)/3. VWAP(t)=sum(tp*volume)/sum(volume) over the session's bars from 00:00 up to and including t. SD(t)=sqrt(sum(volume*(tp-VWAP(t))^2)/sum(volume)) over the same bars. LB(t)=VWAP(t)-2.0*SD(t). SIGNAL WINDOW: only bars opening from 02:00 to 19:45 UTC inclusive can be a tag bar or an entry bar (bars opening 00:00-01:45 and 20:00-23:45 give no tags and no entries). TREND-DAY FILTER: at least one earlier bar of the same session closed above its own VWAP before the tag bar. TAG: a bar k in the signal window with low(k) <= LB(k) that passes the trend-day filter. ENTRY (long) at the close of the first bar t with k+1 <= t <= k+8 (k = the most recent tag, same session) such that close(t) > LB(t) AND close(t) < VWAP(t) AND (VWAP(t)-close(t))/close(t) >= 0.008, and no position is open. Each tag can produce at most one entry; after an exit, a new entry requires a new tag bar after the exit bar. At most 2 entries per session per pair. STOP-LOSS: native fixed stop 1.0% below the entry price, triggered intrabar (this fixed percentage replaces the source's 'lowest low from tag to entry' stop, as the engine requires one fixed percentage). TARGET EXIT: exit signal at the close of the first bar after entry whose close >= VWAP of that bar (current session VWAP), filled at the next open. TIME EXIT: exit at the close of the 23:45 UTC bar (fill at the 00:00 open, before the VWAP reset), and in any case after 48 bars (12 hours) in the trade, whichever comes first. No leverage, spot, long only, one position per pair, whole stake per trade.
rationale: Large orders are executed and benchmarked against the session VWAP. A 2-sigma stretch below it on a day that has already traded above VWAP (so not a one-way trend day) usually comes from a burst of urgent selling (a metaorder, a stop cascade) that liquidity providers absorb at a discount; once the flow pauses, price drifts back toward the volume-weighted fair level. The close back above the lower band marks that pause, and the seller who demanded immediacy pays the liquidity provider's premium. The 0.8% minimum distance from close to VWAP makes the gross target at least 0.8%, well above the 0.30% base / 0.45% conservative round trip; the 1.0% fixed stop keeps losses tight and bounded. Expected frequency: roughly 0.5-1.5 qualifying tags per pair per day on volatile days and none on quiet ones, so about 150-400 trades per year per pair, every one closed within 12 hours (by 00:00 UTC at the latest). The source caveat applies: there is no reliable published win rate; the source only skips trades whose distance to VWAP is below the round-trip cost.
novelty_vs_tried: Anchored to the daily (00:00 UTC) session VWAP with volume-weighted standard-deviation bands, a fade of a measured 2-sigma overshoot with a re-entry trigger and a VWAP target. It differs from WeeklyAnchoredVWAPReclaim (H-041: weekly anchor, a cross/reclaim rule with small moves), from BollingerMeanReversionBaseline (price-only SMA bands, RSI, 1h, no session anchor or volume weighting), from VolumeProfileValueAreaReject (value-area levels, not VWAP sigma bands) and from EMASnapbackATR (EMA/ATR distance, no session reset). It adds a trend-day filter (session must have closed above VWAP) and a minimum 0.8% distance to target so the move per trade exceeds cost.
data_visible_at_proposal: No price data inspected; only research/context/H-086.md (exploration summaries of earlier hypotheses) and the cited web page, as of 2026-11-08.
